verses.zh: （大卫上行之诗。）人对我说：我们往耶和华的殿去，我就欢喜。
verses.en: A song of ascents;[NOTE:1] by David.I was glad because[NOTE:2] they said to me,“We will go to the Lord’s temple.”
notes: Psalm 122. The psalmist expresses his love for Jerusalem and promises to pray for the city’s security.

The precise significance of this title, which appears in Pss 120-134, is unclear. Perhaps worshipers recited these psalms when they ascended the road to Jerusalem to celebrate annual religious festivals. For a discussion of their background see L. C. Allen, Psalms 101-150 (WBC), 219-21.

verses.zh: 耶路撒冷啊，我们的脚站在你的门内。
verses.en: Our feet are[NOTE:1] standinginside your gates, O Jerusalem.
notes: Heb “in the ones saying to me.” After the verb שָׂמַח (samakh), the preposition ב (bet) usually introduces the reason for joy.

verses.zh: 耶路撒冷被建造，如同连络整齐的一座城。
verses.en: Jerusalem[NOTE:1] is a city designedto accommodate an assembly.[NOTE:2]
notes: For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.

verses.zh: 众支派，就是耶和华的支派，上那里去，按以色列的常例（或译：作以色列的证据）称赞耶和华的名。
verses.en: The tribes go up[NOTE:1] there,[NOTE:2] the tribes of the Lord,where it is required that Israelgive thanks to the name of the Lord.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “Jerusalem, which is built like a city which is joined to her together.” The meaning of the Hebrew text is unclear. Many regard this as a description of the compact way in which the city was designed or constructed. The translation assumes an emendation of the verb חֻבְּרָה (khubberah, “is joined”) to a noun חֶבְרָה (khevrah, “association; company”). The text then reads literally, “Jerusalem, which is built like a city which has a company together.” This in turn can be taken as a reference to Jerusalem’s role as a city where people congregated for religious festivals and other civic occasions (see vv. 4-5).
Heb “which is where the tribes go up.”

verses.zh: 因为在那里设立审判的宝座，就是大卫家的宝座。
verses.en: Indeed,[NOTE:1] the leaders sit[NOTE:2] there on thrones and make legal decisions,on the thrones of the house of David.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “[it is] a statute for Israel to give thanks to the name of the Lord.”

verses.zh: 你们要为耶路撒冷求平安！耶路撒冷啊，爱你的人必然兴旺！
verses.en: Pray[NOTE:1] for the peace of Jerusalem.May those who love her prosper.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “Indeed, there they sit [on] thrones for judgment, [on] thrones [belonging] to the house of David.”

verses.zh: 愿你城中平安！愿你宫内兴旺！
verses.en: May there be peace inside your defensesand prosperity[NOTE:1] inside your fortresses.[NOTE:2]

verses.zh: 因我弟兄和同伴的缘故，我要说：愿平安在你中间！
verses.en: For the sake of my brothers and my neighborsI will say, “May there be peace in you.”

verses.zh: 因耶和华―我们　神殿的缘故，我要为你求福！
verses.en: For the sake of the temple of the Lord our GodI will pray for you to prosper.[NOTE:1]
notes: The psalmist uses second feminine singular pronominal forms to address personified Jerusalem.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS ‒ For full note on MT superscriptions, see Psalm 120.

they said to me,

"Let us go to the house of the Lord."

2Our feet are

122:1 "they said to me" This Psalm describes a pilgrimage to the temple, probably on an annual feast day
(cf. Ps. 122:4; Leviticus 23) or special called event.

The "they" would refer to

- fellow pilgrims already on the road to Jerusalem

- local Levites welcoming the pilgrims to Jerusalem

- liturgical imagery

Jerusalem was the "special place" of God's dwelling during the United Monarchy and Divided
Monarchy. After the Babylonian exile and the Jews were allowed to return (i.e., the decree of Cyrus, 538 B.C.),
it became even more precious to the restored Israelites.

SPECIAL TOPIC: FEASTS OF ISRAEL

122:2 The imagery of "feet" or "walking" is part of the theological language of a godly life. God's will was a
clearly revealed path. The ultimate goal was arriving in the presence of God at the temple. This also functioned for the
end-of-life fellowship with God (cf. Job 14:13-17; Ps. 23:4-6).

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE PATH, THE WAY

▣ "Jerusalem" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: MORIAH, SALEM, JEBUS, JERUSALEM, ZION.

122:3 This is an unusual verse. It is difficult to know exactly what is being affirmed or praised. The
VERB (BDB 287, KB 287, Pual PERFECT) basically is used of joining things.
In the Pual stem it denotes

- the two shoulder pieces of the ephod ‒ Exod. 28:7; 39:4

- post-exilic Jerusalem's rapidly built wall ‒ Neh. 4:6

- allies ‒ Ps. 94:20

- people living together ‒ Eccl. 9:4

Here, it seems to denote a well-designed and well-connected city plan. The Jewish Study Bible, p. 1426, suggests
this refers to Nehemiah's time. He had to make the city smaller in order to

- build it rapidly

- have men to guard and protect it

122:4 In Deuteronomy Moses instructs Israel to go to a specific place to worship YHWH (e.g., Deut. 16:16). This
verse alludes to these annual worship gatherings (cf. Leviticus 23).

122:6-9 This strophe denotes a call to prayer.

- Qal IMPERATIVE ‒ Ps. 122:6a

- two JUSSIVES ‒ Ps. 122:6b,7a

- two COHORTATIVES ‒ Ps. 122:8b,9b

Because Jerusalem was the capital of David's Kingdom and the permanent site
of the temple, it had a special place of emphasis in the OT.

However, I think the NT has universalized the national promises to Israel to include all
humanity. The focus of biblical faith is no longer the temple in Jerusalem but the new and superior temple in Jesus
(see the book of Hebrews). Neither Jesus or any Apostle ever reaffirms the national, geographical promises to Israel.
I know this is different from what you read/hear from many authors/preachers, seminaries. Please check the following
Special Topics before you reject this theological assertion.

-
SPECIAL TOPIC: WHY DO OT COVENANT PROMISES SEEM SO DIFFERENT FROM NT COVENANT PROMISES?

-
SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

122:6 "peace" The term (see
SPECIAL TOPIC: PEACE [shalom]), "peace" (BDB 1022) forms part of the name "Jerusalem." Remember,
the site of the temple was Mt. Moriah (cf. Genesis 22). In Genesis 14 it is called "Salem." These word plays are not so
much etymological as sound plays in Hebrew, but the words are not Hebrew.

Notice the number of sound plays in Ps. 122:6.

- pray שׁאל ‒ (BDB 981, KB 1371)

- peace שׁלום ‒ (BDB 1022)

- Jerusalem ורישׁםל ‒ (BDB 436)

- prosper שׁלה ‒ (BDB 1017, KB 1503)

▣ "May they prosper who love you" This type of phrase is often used of "Prosperity Gospel"
preachers to give biblical evidence of a promise. Please see the booklet by my favorite charismatic scholar,
Gordon Fee, The Disease of the Health, Wealth Gospels.
